nodes.title: Counting integers with a given least prime factor in an interval

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the iterated remainder set $S_1(n)$ equals the remainder set $S(n) = \{n \bmod k : 1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor\}$.
nodes.title: The first iterated remainder set is the remainder set

nodes.summary: The iterated remainder sets of $35$ satisfy $S_6(35) = \{0\}$ and $S_7(35) = \emptyset$.
nodes.title: Iterated remainder sets of 35

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the iterated remainder sets $S_j(n)$, $j \ge 0$, are defined by $S_0(n) = \{1, \dots, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor\}$ and, for $j \ge 0$, $S_{j+1}(n) = \{n \bmod k : k \in S_j(n),\ k \ne 0\}$.
nodes.title: Iterated remainder sets

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $t$ be natural numbers, let $P(n)$ be the maximal Pierce length of $n$ and let $S_j(n)$ be the iterated remainder sets of $n$. Then the following are equivalent: $P(n) = t + 1$; $S_t(n) = \{0\}$; $S_t(n)$ has exactly one element and $S_{t+j}(n) = \emptyset$ for every $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Maximal Pierce length via iterated remainder sets

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the number $\pi(n)$ of primes at most $n$ satisfies $\pi(n) \le 1.3\, n / \log n$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Upper bound $1.3\, n / \log n$ for the prime-counting function

nodes.summary: The remainder-set constant is $c = \sum_{p} \frac{1}{p(p+1)} \prod_{q < p} \left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)$, where $p$ runs over all primes and, for each $p$, $q$ runs over the primes less than $p$.
nodes.title: The remainder-set constant

nodes.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ and let $c$ be the remainder-set constant. Then, as $n \to \infty$ over the natural numbers, $s(n) - cn = O\bigl(n / (\log n \cdot \log \log n)\bigr)$, and $s(n)/n \to c$.
nodes.title: Asymptotic formula for the number of remainders

nodes.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Then $s(n+1) \le s(n) + 1$ for every $n \ge 1$; there is a real constant $C$ with $s(n) - C \log \log n \le s(n+1)$ for all sufficiently large $n$; and for every natural number $M$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $s(n+1) + M \le s(n)$, that is, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} (s(n+1) - s(n)) = -\infty$.
nodes.title: Consecutive differences of the number of remainders

nodes.summary: Let $s(n)$ be the number of distinct remainders $n \bmod k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. For every natural number $M$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $s(n+1) + M \le s(n)$; equivalently, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} (s(n+1) - s(n)) = -\infty$.
nodes.title: Unbounded drops in the number of remainders

nodes.summary: The number $s(11)$ of distinct remainders $11 \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le 5$ equals $4$.
nodes.title: The remainder count of 11

nodes.summary: The number $s(12)$ of distinct remainders $12 \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le 6$ equals $2$.
nodes.title: The remainder count of 12

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $s(n)$ is the number of elements of the remainder set $S(n)$, that is, the number of distinct values of $n \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ (OEIS A283190).
nodes.title: Remainder count

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the remainder set is $S(n) = \{\, n \bmod k : 1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \,\}$, the set of remainders of $n$ modulo the integers from $1$ to $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Remainder set

nodes.summary: As the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, the sum $\sum_{p > n,\ p \text{ prime}} 1/p^2$ of the inverse squares of the primes greater than $n$ is $O(1/(n \log n))$.
nodes.title: Tail of the sum of inverse prime squares

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
